category_title: Students who engage in disruptive off-task behavior to access peer attention
minimal_context: Craig is supposed to be completing a reading assignment during independent work time in a general classroom setting with cluster seating.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please start your independent work on the reading assignment. We will be working quietly for the next fifteen minutes.

STUDENT: (Turns to a peer at his cluster) Did you guys watch that new movie that came out yesterday?

TUTOR: Craig, remember the rules for independent work.

STUDENT: Okay. (Pauses, then leans over to another peer) Are you going to the park after school?

TUTOR: Craig, you need to stop talking and do your work.

STUDENT: (Laughs as a peer responds back) I know, right? Hey, what level did you get to on that game last night?

options.A: Implement relatively tight timelines for Craig to complete his reading assignment during independent work time.
options.B: Provide Craig with access to more socially appropriate sensory stimulation by giving him a squishy stress ball during independent work time.
options.C: Proactively contact Craig's parents to share both successes and concerns regarding his behavior during independent work time.
options.D: Teach Craig to use business-size appointment cards with a checklist of choices to access peer attention during designated times.
